name: What is the best way to fill in a pool after removal?

mainEntity.name: Which fill material and compaction method creates the most stable finished yard?
mainEntity.text: Which fill material and compaction method creates the most stable finished yard?

acceptedAnswer.text: The quality of the fill process determines whether the yard remains stable after the pool is gone. The cavity should be filled in layers, with each lift compacted before the next one goes in. Clean fill or approved engineered material is preferred over mixed debris or poorly screened soil. If the area will support landscaping only, standard backfill may be enough when it is placed and compacted correctly. If the space may later support a patio, walkway, or structure, the fill and compaction standard should be more demanding. Homeowners should ask what material will be used, how thick each lift will be, and whether any compaction testing is included. Weak fill is one of the main causes of future settling, so the cheapest dirt is rarely the best choice.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best fill method uses clean soil or engineered fill placed in layers and compacted as the cavity is filled. Proper compaction matters more than using the cheapest dirt because weak fill can settle later and create dips or drainage problems.
